text:
devin: Heads-up — nightly bench found a weird numeric/ perf regression in the new paged/ fused-flash variant. Some batches hit inf/NaN from the softmax step when sequence length + KV pages > ~3000. Attn outputs clipped to inf and downstream sampling exploded. Posting quick repro + profiler snippets.

maggie: ugh. repro script? small input that triggers it?

devin: minimal repro is in the thread: run bench-attn-range.py with --pages 3 --seq 1100 --dtype bf16 --batch 4. Crash appears nondet (only ~1/20 runs).

devin: nvprof excerpt:
```
GPU activities: 98% time in custom_flash_attn_kernel (fp16 path) then fallback path on some batches -> fallback_bf16_softmax_kernel: huge reduction time spike
Warp-level reductions show many replays and a single block with very large max logits ~1.2e4
```

raj: first thought: page-boundary accumulation. If we compute softmax per page but don't do a stable global normalization across pages we can get extremely large intermediate logits. BF16 has small dynamic range so exponent can overflow.

linh: agreed. two mitigation ideas: 1) stable log-sum-exp across pages (carry the running max + running sum of exp shifted by max) 2) per-head clamp of logits to a safe range (we used [-50, 50] for earlier fp16 paths). Both fix numerics but differ in perf.

devin: tried LSE-accumulate approach: fixes NaNs, but perf regressed ~8% on A100 for fp16 baseline, and ~14% for bf16 path. Bench numbers below (median of 5 runs):

| variant | p50 latency (ms) | tokens/sec | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| old-flash (fp16) | 12.3 | 82k | baseline |
| fused-paged (bf16) | 11.8 | 85k | before overflow |
| fused-paged + LSE | 12.7 | 78k | numeric-stable: no NaNs |
| fused-paged + clamp(-50,50) | 12.1 | 83k | small perf hit, solved many cases |

maggie: clamp seems like a good cheap fix. But is it semantically safe? Are we changing model outputs?

raj: clamp does change distribution a bit for extreme logits, but those extremes are already numerically invalid. We should add a regression test set with golden completions and compute acceptance thresholds. If outputs shift beyond tolerance, we rollback.

infra-bot: nightly-run: paged-attn-regression detected on bench-attn-range (id: pr-8342) — failing 2/30 runs; alerting eng-runtime.

linh: other angle: kernel selection heuristic. We can add a quick preflight: scan max(logits) estimate per block (cheap reduce) and if estimated range > threshold, route to stable-LSE kernel; else use fast path. That minimizes perf hit by only triggering on bad batches.

devin: implemented a prototype threshold check (one warp reduce) and it switches to stable kernel when max_logit - min_logit > 40. Results: false positives ~1% (extra cost), catches all NaN cases, net perf ~+3% vs always-LSE but still -2% vs pure fast path.

sre-jen: from rollout perspective, we should canary this. Add feature flag to runtime to enable threshold-based kernel switch per model route. Canary on dedicated infra first -> then small subset of hosted. Also add alerting when switch_rate > 5% for a route.

devin: added metrics: attn_kernel_choice{model,route} with labels fast|stable|clamp. Dashboard draft: per-model switch rate, avg latency delta, downstream output-drift (bertscore vs golden).

maggie: tests: please add litmus prompts that stress prefixes and long-context prompts. Include some randomized heavy-logit prompts to exercise exp tails. Put them under eng-runtime/tests/attn_numerics/ as part of CI.

ci-bot: CI job nightly-attn-numerics queued. Expect runtime regression test to run in < 6h.

raj: KV cache behavior note: when pages are merged on KV-side we sometimes produce slightly different q/k alignment which amplifies logits for a few heads — that can push already-large logit ranges past overflow. Need to audit our KV page concat code: ensure we do a stable dtype cast and avoid accumulating rounding errors across concatenations.

linh: practical plan summary:
- short term: clamp logits at [-60, 60] as emergency guard in fused kernel (low perf cost).
- medium: deploy threshold-based kernel switch with optimized warp-level LSE.
- long term: refactor paged KV concat to preserve numeric stability + add golden prompt suite for numeric regression detection.

devin: created PR with clamp + feature-flag + metrics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987. Wrote microbench harness and added flame profiler snapshots. Requesting reviews from @maggie @raj.

maggie: reviewing now. If we land clamp behind flag and roll out canary with switch-rate alerting, I think it's safe. Add changelog note about numeric-clamp behavior and impact on outputs.

devin: thanks — will open a follow-up to add LSE-warp optimized kernel (C++/CUDA) and unit tests. Leaving this thread open for bench updates. :thumbsup:
